phase3_findings.description: The wider require_base_tables duty for custom runners (refuse child tables, calls matching database-defined routines, failed catalog lookups) is enforced only by documentation; RlsGuardRunner.__init__ checks only the parameter name.
_refuse_database_routines treats every non-postgres dialect as MySQL; the postgres/mysql precondition is enforced only by its caller and is not stated in the function or docstring.
The PostgreSQL pg_class row is read by position (row[0], row[1:3], row[3]); the child-flag meaning depends on the SELECT list order. Fails closed today.

The _called_names docstring (and docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md line 45) says strpos is emitted as POSITION; the PR's own test comment says the rewrite emits STRPOS on sqlglot 25.x and POSITION on 30.x, and the project allows sqlglot>=25.0,<31.

Ambiguous sentence 'no collected name skips the query' in the internal RLS doc; the code skips the routine lookup when no name is collected. 'One parameterized query per statement' means per verify_base_tables call.

The verify_base_tables fail-closed handler now also catches routine-lookup and tokenizer failures but still logs and returns a message about a relation-type check; for a relation-free call the message names a check that never ran.

The routine check runs only for dialect postgres or mysql; for any other dialect a relation-free call passes unchecked, while _verify_relations raises RlsError for an unknown dialect. No shipped runner reaches this.

_called_names sends each name as written, lower-cased and ASCII-only lower-cased; no test pins all three spellings because _FakeCatalog lower-cases every parameter and connector tests use ASCII names only.
The changelog.d/325.security.md fragment required by acceptance criterion twelve is missing; the diff adds no changelog.d file.
test_untokenizable_or_unparsable_sql_fails_closed uses inputs that fail inside _relations before _called_names runs, so the _called_names tokenizer failure path is never reached by a test.

_FakeCatalog.execute dispatches with sql.startswith('SET ') and splits a qualified name with .split('.'), string handling the repository's sqlglot rule names (test fake over fixed catalog queries only).

## Verdict: REJECT (acceptance criterion twelve unmet: the changelog fragment is missing)

The code change is sound and fails closed, but this PR is not ready to merge because it does not add the `changelog.d/325.security.md` release-note fragment that acceptance criterion twelve requires.

Rule applied: unmet-decided-criterion carve-out (Important finding one), together with rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold (VC-55) → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🔴 Critical

- VC-55: FAIL (critical) — A `changelog.d/<PR>.security.md` fragment states the outcome and the operator action: query top-level tables and move child rules to the parent, and note that, under RLS, calls to PostgreSQL functions outside `pg_catalog`/`information_schema` and to MySQL stored functions are blocked, and that while rules are active the read-only guard's function blocklist applies even when `database.read_only` is false. `changelog.d/274.security.md` is unchanged. [changelog.d] — fix the code, or have the issue author amend this criterion

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  criteria.json counts (criterion 12 present, well-formed list). The diff contains no changelog.d path (grep 'changelog\.d' on diff.patch: no matches). The head view's changelog.d security fragments (+legacy-001, +legacy-002, 274, 280, 288) are identical in set to the base view's; no new <PR>.security.md exists. The only fragment mentioning pg_inherits/blocklist/stored function is the pre-existing 274.security.md, which the criterion says must stay unchanged. So the required new fragment (child-table operator action, function-call blocking on PostgreSQL/MySQL, blocklist applying with read_only false) is absent. 274.security.md is unchanged, but that is only half of the criterion.

  </details>

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. The required release-note fragment `changelog.d/325.security.md` is missing. Acceptance criterion twelve asks for a security fragment that tells operators to query top-level tables and move child-table rules to the parent, and that says PostgreSQL functions outside `pg_catalog`/`information_schema` and MySQL stored functions are blocked under RLS, and that the function blocklist applies while rules are active even when `database.read_only` is false. The diff adds no file under `changelog.d/`, and the head view holds the same fragment set as the base. (raised by 1/6 agents) [unmet-decided-criterion carve-out] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=not-held limb-one=not-evaluated limb-two=not-evaluated; evidence: scripts/changelog.py reads changelog.d fragments to generate CHANGELOG.md (line 54) and refuses a release while fragments are unconsumed (line 118), so adding the fragment changes that tool's output and branch -->

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (11)

<details><summary>11 items</summary>

1. The `_called_names` docstring in `src/sqllens/safety/relations.py` (lines 88-89) says `strpos` "is emitted as `POSITION`", and `docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md` line 45 says the same. The PR's own test comment in `tests/unit/test_rls_views.py` says the rewrite emits `STRPOS` on sqlglot 25.x and `POSITION` on 30.x, and the project allows `sqlglot>=25.0,<31`. So the example holds only on part of the supported range. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: the sentence describes sqlglot output and no code branches on it; no .sh, .py, .jq or workflow consumer reads the docstring or the internal page; the docstring is never printed and the internal doc page is not published -->
2. In `docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md` line 45, the sentence "no collected name skips the query" can be read two ways. The code means that the routine lookup is skipped when no call name is collected (`if called:` in `verify_base_tables`). "One parameterized query per statement" also means one per `verify_base_tables` call, that is, per SQL text. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: wording only, no code branches on it; no tool reads this internal page; it is not published -->
3. The fail-closed handler in `src/sqllens/safety/relations.py` (lines 137-145) now also catches failures of the routine lookup and of the call-name tokenizer, but it still logs "row-level-security relation check raised" and returns "row-level security could not verify relation types; query blocked". For a statement with no relation reference, such as `SELECT fn()` with the `pg_proc` or `ROUTINES` grant revoked, both the client message and the log name a check that never ran. `docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md` line 47 repeats the same wording. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. In `src/sqllens/safety/relations.py` (lines 124-126), the routine check runs only when the dialect is `postgres` or `mysql`. For any other dialect string, a statement with no relation reference returns without any check, while `_verify_relations` raises `RlsError` for an unknown dialect. No shipped runner reaches this, because the three runners pass `sqlite`, `postgres` or `mysql`, but a custom runner beneath `RlsGuardRunner` would get this open default. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `_refuse_database_routines` in `src/sqllens/safety/relations.py` (lines 222-247) treats every dialect other than `postgres` as MySQL in its `else` branch. Only its one caller enforces that the dialect is `postgres` or `mysql`, and neither the function nor its docstring states the rule. It still fails closed through the outer `except Exception`. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. `_called_names` in `src/sqllens/safety/relations.py` (lines 104-106) sends each name three ways: as written, lower-cased, and with only ASCII letters lower-cased. No test pins all three: `_FakeCatalog` lower-cases every parameter before matching, and the connector tests use only ASCII names. Dropping the ASCII-only form would pass every test, although it would let an unquoted non-ASCII PostgreSQL function name miss the `pg_proc` match on a database whose `lower()` does not fold non-ASCII letters. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. `test_untokenizable_or_unparsable_sql_fails_closed` in `tests/unit/test_rls_views.py` (lines 646-647) uses two inputs that both fail inside `_relations` (`sqlglot.parse_one`) before `_called_names` runs. So the tokenizer call in `_called_names` has a stated failure path but no test that reaches it. The outcome is still fail-closed, because `_relations` tokenizes the same SQL under the same dialect first. (raised by 1/6 agents)
8. The new `_FakeCatalog.execute` test helper in `tests/unit/test_rls_views.py` (lines 477-482) dispatches with `sql.startswith("SET ")` and splits a qualified name with `.split(".")`. It handles only the guard's own fixed catalog queries, not untrusted SQL, but it uses the string handling the repository's sqlglot rule names. (raised by 1/6 agents)
9. The wider `require_base_tables` duty described in `src/sqllens/agent/capabilities/sql_runner/base.py` (lines 30-34) is enforced only by documentation. `RlsGuardRunner.__init__` checks only the parameter name, so it cannot tell whether a custom runner performs the new child and routine checks. No shipped runner is affected, and the docs already disclose that a runner which ignores the keyword cannot be detected. (raised by 1/6 agents)
10. In `src/sqllens/safety/relations.py` (lines 166-189), the PostgreSQL catalog row is read by position (`row[0]`, `row[1:3]`, `row[3]`), so the child-flag meaning depends on the SELECT list order. A missing column or a non-boolean flag already fails closed. (raised by 1/6 agents)

checklist.verify_hint: Trace inputs that could reach execution without the name being collected: a MySQL versioned comment such as `SELECT /*!50000 stored_fn() */ 1` (sqlglot drops comments but MySQL executes the body), a call name tokenized as neither VAR/IDENTIFIER nor a KEYWORDS entry, and a non-ASCII name whose PostgreSQL lower() differs from Python's lower()
checklist.evidence: Docstring at relations.py:117-120 matches the code path (_called_names 84-107 feeding _refuse_database_routines 222-252, run even with no relations at 125-132). Checked hint vectors: MySQL versioned comments are rejected earlier by readonly.py:505-506 (not by this module); quoted/keyword/VAR names are collected (101-106); PostgreSQL non-ASCII is covered by text, lower and ASCII-lower variants with proname = ANY and lower(proname) = ANY (236). Open risk not settled by reading: sqlglot Postgres tokenizer only supports U&' string escapes (sqlglot/dialects/postgres.py:90), so a Unicode-escaped quoted identifier call such as U&"\0066n"(1) would likely tokenize to VAR U, &, IDENTIFIER with raw text \0066n, which would not match the routine fn that PostgreSQL decodes to; likewise MySQL routine names use an accent-insensitive collation while the match is LOWER(...) IN (...) on exact text. I did not run parse_one/tokenize or a live database to confirm these, and I did not confirm that the read-only guard lets such statements through, so neither FAIL nor PASS is established.
